open_problems.problem: No matched 10k/12.5k/15k evaluation for v2.4.2; 15k is latest, not best.
Semantic quality at v2.4.2 10k remained weak; 15k quality is unknown.
Validation loss bottomed near 11k and ended higher at 15k.
Core train.py resume checks variant/model config but does not hard-fail on tokenizer SHA or dataset identity.
Core checkpoint step writes do not have the full atomic write and reload verification used by Colab tooling.
SFT execution is fragmented between finetune.py and safer specialized runners.
Wikisource has no validation allocation and the corpus remains 54.39% literary.
README and glyph.maksu.online model copy are stale relative to the v2.4.2 15k training snapshot.
Public demo serves Glyph-27M step 115k; the reason for that exact checkpoint is not documented.
Workspace is not a Git repository and pytest is absent from the local virtual environment.

next_steps.action: Generate the final 10k-to-15k run report and matched evaluation of v2.4.2 checkpoints at 10k, 12.5k and 15k without training.
Select and record a canonical v2.4.2 best checkpoint, then compare it with v2.3.1 44k using the same prompts and decoding.
Only after evaluation decide whether to stop, retain 10k/12.5k, or authorize a controlled 20k checkpoint with a reviewed LR schedule.
Add hard resume checks for tokenizer SHA and dataset identity, atomic verified checkpoint writes, and consolidate the safe SFT runner.
Align README, glyph.maksu.online content and dashboard metadata; explicitly label the public demo as archival Glyph-27M step 115k.
Address the Wikisource validation gap and literary bias before another large corpus rebuild; do not scale SFT v0.3.
